but Jesus is bigger and he's powerful and he's mighty.
and he can save us out of all the challenges of our life..
It's good for us to say that to each other..
It's healthy..
It encourages us..
It keeps us going..
Worship and praise is so good for us emotionally..
It's so good for us physically..
It's so good for us spiritually..
And then the last thing we see here.
is that we worship and praise.
because it's a witness to others..
Some of the earliest second century texts.
talking about the early church.
agree that the worship gatherings of the early church.
that happened on Sunday were first and foremost.
what they called Eucharistia or Thanksgiving..
That was what defined those gatherings.
was that they were about thanksgiving to God..
Worship and praise to God and talking about who God is.
and how good he is and exalting him.
and talking about his work in our lives.
has always been a defining characteristic.
of the church of Christians from the very, very beginning..
In the second century,.
there was this pagan writer named Celsus.
who didn't like Christians..
He was a critic of the church..
He was writing to someone else.
and he commented in this letter.
that he didn't like Christian worship.
because the chants and the songs that they sang.
were unfamiliar to his ears,.
but they were also so beautiful.
that he felt that they dulled his reasoning faculties.
and made him more open to the Christian arguments..
From the very beginning,.

$^{481}$we as a people, followers of Jesus,.
have been known as people who worship.
and sing and sing beautifully..
That doesn't mean that we all necessarily.
know how to play instruments or even sing on key,.
but it's beautiful because it comes from our hearts.
and it's genuine and it's worship to God..
That's been a part of who we are from the very beginning.
and it's a part of who we are now..
In Acts 2, verses 46 and 47, it says this..
Day by day, attending the temple together.
and breaking bread in their homes,.
they received their food with glad and generous heart,.
praising God and having favor with the people.
and the Lord added to their number day by day.
those who were being saved..
That was the very first church..
Every day, they were getting together,.
doing different things and one of the things.
they were doing was praising God..
And one of the powerful things about worship.
is that genuine worship and praise to God,.
it can't be duplicated or counterfeited in the world..
We see that in American culture..
We have this beautiful tradition of gospel music.
in the US that comes from the African American church..
Well, there's a difference between someone.
singing that song in church.
and someone just singing it on the stage.
at an award show who doesn't know Jesus..
It's two totally different things..
You can't counterfeit genuine worship.
and the world around us notices that too..
It's a witness..
When we are genuinely worshiping God,.
they say that's something beautiful.
and that's an expression that you don't find anywhere else..
It can't be duplicated..
And genuine worship and praise to God.
is always focused on God, not on us.

$^{521}$and that's another reason it's a witness..
Genuine worship and praise to God.
is some form of saying, listen, this is who I was.
and then this is who God made me or is making me to be..
This is my present situation.
but this is what God has for me..
This is what my future used to be.
but now because of Jesus, this is what is in my future..
Those types of statements define our worship.
where we're saying, look, it's about God..
God did this..
It's not about me..
The focus is on him and how good he is.
and how great he is and all that he's done in my life..
That's what we see in these verses three to 14.
of Ephesians one..
And that type of worship is always a witness to other people..
The people around us, they may think it's strange,.
they may think it's unusual but they'll notice it.
and people will say, that's different..
What are you talking about?.
Why are you talking about it?.
Why are you joyful?.
Why are you talking about your God.
even when life is terrible and I can see that it's terrible.
and you're going through a time of lament.
but you're still worshiping in that?.
Those things are all a witness to the people around us..
So I wanna close out with application for us..
Like I said, this passage gives us.
this beautiful expression of worship..
It's a great template for us to think about.
and it makes it clear that this should be a part.
of our lifestyle and clearly in the church,.
just like we worship this morning,.
but it should be a part of our lifestyle every day..
We should verbally be praising God,.
talking to ourselves, nothing wrong with talking to yourself.
if you're gonna preach the gospel.
or talk about who God is to yourself..

$^{561}$That's a healthy, good thing..
We should be doing that,.
especially when we're going through difficult times..
We should be telling ourselves, you know what?.
It's hard but God's at work in my life..
God loves me, I'm forgiven, I'm redeemed..
That should be a part of our life rhythm..
But I know it's not always easy..
So how do we do that?.
How do we make that happen?.
I want us to think about something for just a minute..
To illustrate this, we can take a mental excursion real fast.
so let's pretend, you know, if you go down Halsted here.
to 31st and then you just go east on 31st,.
as far east as you can go, you get to the lake.
and there's the beach park there, right?.
Everybody been to 31st Street Beach?.
And it's a really pretty beach park..
There's that point out there where the marina is..
You can walk out there and they have kind of.
these big boulders for breakwater..
You can look back towards the city..
If you haven't done it, you should do it sometime..
It's a really, really cool spot..
It's a great spot to take pictures of the skyline..
But if you go out there and if I asked each one of you.
to describe what you would see when you're there,.
your answers would vary depending on how you were oriented..
If you're looking straight east from out there,.
all you're gonna see is water..
You're just gonna see the lake, which is beautiful..
That's all you're gonna see..
If you're looking back to the west,.
then you're gonna see the city skyline..
You're gonna see Lakeshore Drive..
You're gonna see something totally, totally different.
depending on how you're oriented..
And I think that's really instructive for us in worship,.
especially when we're struggling to worship..
We're saying, I know I need more worship in my life..

$^{601}$I wanna express praise to God,.
but it's not coming naturally right now..
I don't feel it..
We need to think about what are we oriented towards..
And sometimes in life, we need to turn the eyes of our soul.
away from our problems, away from our success,.
away from our failures, away from our relationships,.
away from our entertainment,.
away from all our social media feeds,.
and say, I'm gonna orient myself towards God..
I'm gonna look at God..
I'm gonna behold God..
And we do that as we look in His word..
We do that as we look into our hearts.
and recount God's grace in our life..
And we say, you know what?.
This is what God has done for me,.
and this is what God has done in the past..
Or we look at the lives of other believers around us.
and say, I see God doing this in someone else's life,.
and it's a beautiful thing..
I see something encouraging happening.
with a brother or sister..
When we do those things, we begin to orient ourselves.
towards looking at God..
And when we look at God, then we can begin to worship..
The scripture talks about this..
Psalm 75, one says, we give thanks to you, O God..
We give thanks for your name is near..
We recount your wondrous deeds..
Psalm 124, one says, if it had not been the Lord.
who was on our side, let Israel now say..
And so I would challenge and encourage all of us.
to do that and to seek ways to do that in our lives..
Begin to orient our soul towards looking at God..
There's a lot of stuff for us to look at in the world..
Way too much..
We can't take it all in..
And sometimes we need to turn away from those things.
and orient ourselves towards God..

$^{641}$And if we'll do that, it'll be so good for us..
It'll be life for us..
It'll be life-giving..
It'll be a witness to those around us..
And ultimately, it's an identity that God has given you.
as one of his children, is to worship him as a worshiper..
That's who we are..
We are worshipers..
Let's pray..
God, we thank you for your greatness..
We thank you for your grace..
We thank you for who you are,.
all that you have done in redemption..
We thank you for all that you have done in our lives,.
and we are undeserving..
We need you desperately, God..
And God, you love us and have redeemed us and forgiven us..
I pray that you would help all of us.
to orient our souls to look at that,.
to look at you, to look at what you've done for us,.
to look at your grace, and may worship come out of us..
In Jesus' name, amen..

$^{1}$Good morning, everyone..
It is great to be here on another Sunday morning with all of you to worship with you, to take.
communion with you, and to just enjoy the presence of this family that we've been adopted.
into..
If I could, let me open us in a word of prayer..
Would you bow your heads with me as we pray?.
Our Heavenly Father, our Lord, and our God, we come before you today not by what we have.
done, not by our own merit, but because you saw us first and you loved us first, Lord,.
and you have brought us into your presence..
And so, God, this Sunday morning we give to you, I ask that you would just calm our hearts,.
Lord, and give us minds that are focused..
Would you clear away the clouds of sleep, of the troubles of this week?.
Would you focus our attention upon you?.
And so for that, Lord, I ask that you would be with me, that you would speak through me,.
and would you protect the ears of my brothers and sisters as they listen to what I say about.
your word?.
Would you help them remember your word and your word alone?.
All these things we pray in Jesus' name, amen..
Okay, so we'll be continuing our reading of James today, this letter from the Apostle.
James to the Jewish Christians of the dispersion, where he calls for his brothers and sisters.
to live lives according to the faith that they profess..
To be more than just believers in name, but also believers in their living..
In James' words, Christians cannot just be hearers of the word of God, you and I must.
also be doers..
Last week, we saw in chapter 2, verses 14 to 26, that it is a living faith that saves..
That a faith which is without works, without any impact on a person's life, is like trying.
to live without breathing..
It's a life that's incomplete, missing an essential part, an essential aspect, and it.
is one that cannot sustain you..
It's wrong to live in this way, and it's impossible to live in this way..
The only outcome from a faith without works is death..
And so, James calls for his brothers and sisters to have a complete faith and be complete people..
He wants his fellow believers to be perfect, affected by their faith and transformed so.
that their entire being both agrees and works in cohesive wisdom and righteousness..
Toward that end, we are brought to the next part of his letter to his displaced brothers.
and sisters..
If you have your Bibles with you, I invite you to turn with me to the book of James,.
it's third chapter, verses 1 to 12..
Again, that is James chapter 3, verses 1 to 12..
If you don't have a Bible with you this morning, they'll be right here..

$^{41}$So let's read, all right?.
James chapter 3, verses 1 to 12..
Not many of you should become teachers, my fellow believers, because you know that we.
who teach will be judged more strictly..
We all stumble in many ways..
Anyone who is never at fault in what they say is perfect, able to keep their whole body.
in check..
When we put bits in the mouths of horses and make them obey us, we can turn the whole animal..
Or take ships as an example..
Although they are so large and are driven by strong winds, they are steered by a very.
small rudder wherever the pilot wants to go..
Likewise, the tongue is a small part of the body, but it makes great boasts..
Consider what a great forest is set on fire by a small spark..
The tongue also is a fire, a world of evil among the parts of the body..
It corrupts the whole body, sets the whole course of one's life on fire, and is itself.
set on fire by hell..
All kinds of animals, birds, reptiles, and sea creatures are being tamed and have been.
tamed by mankind, but no human being can tame the tongue..
It is a restless evil, full of deadly poison..
With the tongue, we praise our Lord and Father, and with it, we curse human beings who have.
been made in God's likeness..
Out of the same mouth come praise and cursing..
My brothers and sisters, this should not be..
Can both fresh water and fresh water be the same?.
My brothers and sisters, can a fig tree bear olives or a grapevine bear figs?.
Neither can a salt spring produce fresh water..
Do you want to be what James calls his brothers and sisters to be?.
A person who is wise and complete and whole?.
A person perfected by their faith?.
Here in James chapter 3, verses 1 to 12, we see the centrality of the tongue in being.
perfect..
He starts off this chapter by advising caution when considering a position of teaching among.
believers, right?.
Verses 1 to 2, "Not many of you should become teachers, my fellow believers, because you.
know that we who teach will be judged more strictly..
We all stumble in many ways..
Someone who is never at fault in what they say is perfect..
It would keep their whole body in check.".
In speaking about strict judgment, we begin to think about the standard of God..
It's the standard of perfection..

$^{81}$And what James states is that among the many ways in which we fail to keep this standard,.
we most commonly and often fail through what we say..
We are prone to mistakes, and one great maker of mistakes is our tongue, to the point where.
James says that perfection in speech translates to perfection in character..
There's a correlation being drawn between a self-controlled tongue and a self-controlled.
body..
So you see in verses 1 to 2 that the tongue is important, that the tongue holds a key.
place in the direction of your living..
In order to help us understand this, James gives us two illustrations in verses 3 and.
4, a horse and a boat..
There we go..
If we put bits into the mouths of horses so that they obey us, we guide their whole bodies.
as well..
Look at the ships also..
Though they are so large and are driven by strong winds, they are guided by a very small.
rudder wherever the will of a pilot directs..
That is a different version, but here we have two examples..
One is a living creature, the other is a man-made vehicle..
These are large things..
Horses and boats move with immense power..
Have you ever seen a horse?.
Anyone?.
They're big..
Okay, I don't know how else to describe them, but they are much bigger than I pictured them.
to be..
When we quantify the strength of modern-day machinery, what do we use?.
What sort of word do we use?.
We use the word "horsepower" because horses are this measurement of strength..
We tell people, "This machine has this many horses' worth of power.".
By using a bit, which is a metal rod that fits across the inside of a horse's mouth,.
we're able to steer the horse..
We're able to cue and direct the horse in the direction that we want..
A small tug lets the horse know which direction it should turn..
The entire body of the horse is guided by this bit, and it's the same with a boat..
We're given this imagery by James of a large boat driven by strong winds, although they.
are so large and are driven by strong winds..
It's a large boat..
This boat is able to withstand the force of nature..
It takes the power of these air currents to be pushed across the waters..
And yet, using a rudder, a pilot is able to influence and change the direction of that.

$^{121}$force..
The boat is steered by the will of the pilot..
And so we're given these examples to help us understand the effect of words..
Because the tongue holds a key place in the direction of their living..
It is the means by which even a body of great size is directed and controlled..
It is a small member of the body, but it makes great claims, which turns the body in unholy.
and ungodly directions..
If you would look with me at James chapter 3, verse 5, it's on the screen right here..
Likewise, the tongue is a small part of the body, but it makes great boasts..
Consider what a great forest is set on fire by a small spark..
The tongue boasts..
It makes claims, it oversteps, and it speaks in ill ways..
We see in verse 5 through the idea of boasting that this small part of the body is not leading.
its bearer in the good directions..
There is not a proper helmsman at the wheel of this ship..
Instead of works of mercy and compassion, there is only death and destruction..
What a great forest is set on fire by a small spark..
You know, since earlier this year, I think it was around March and April, there have.
been a lot of wildfires consuming Canada..
And I think Chicago got a brief taste of this smoke and ash..
It drifted in over from the north..
And now what I read, this was in August, around August, I read was that the wildfires had.
burned up 37.8 million acres of land..
That is a lot of land..
And something interesting to go with that is that a good portion of these fires were.
started by dry thunderstorms..
It's this lightning produced by the dry environment that sparks these small fires..
Fires which spread across dried out vegetation in the blink of an eye, blazing into these.
massive uncontrollable conflagrations..
They're uncontrollable..
They grow faster than they can be put out and they destroy and displace with no regard.
for anyone and anything..
James describes the tongue as a fire, not just an object that steers, that changes your.
direction, but a fire that wreaks havoc on everything around it..
The tongue is also a fire, a world of evil among the parts of the body..
It corrupts the whole body, sets the whole course of one's life on fire..
Look at that statement in the first sentence of verse six..
The tongue is a world of evil..
The present reality of wrongdoing in this world and all the unrighteousness of that.
world occurs and it finds its representation in the tongue..

$^{161}$The tongue is the part of our bodies which is used by God's enemy to do harm..
James points at it as a manifestation of evil that corrupts the whole body, the entire body,.
the part which directs the rest of our body towards a life of evil and destruction..
It is set on fire by hell..
These are harsh words, scary words..
James looks at the tongue as a power for evil..
And so our tongues, holding a key position in the direction of our living, more often.
than not directs us towards evil..
Have you ever been in a situation where you found yourself processing hurt or anger?.
We're human beings..
Of course we have..
Maybe in those situations we find friends or family to vent our thoughts to..
Maybe we even sit and mutter to ourselves going over and over again and again how the.
offense happened..
But in that process we find that we work ourselves up into a rage..
We get angrier and angrier or more and more upset as we hear our own words, not just our.
spoken words, but also our thoughts as we revisit them over and over again..
And then sometimes we even begin to take it out on the people around us and transgress.
against our brothers and sisters..
The tongue, our words, influence us..
They stain and they spread..
The tongue corrupts the whole body, causing our hands and feet to stumble..
And there is terrible news beyond this..
If you would look with me to verses seven and eight..
All kinds of animals, birds, and reptiles, and sea creatures are being tamed and have.
been tamed by mankind..
But no human being can tame the tongue..
It is a restless evil full of deadly poison..
Think about how mankind has transformed all the things around us to suit our purposes..
The multitude of animals that have been domesticated for our benefit..
Consider the blessing and command of God to Adam and Eve to subdue the earth and to have.
dominion over the fish of the sea and the birds in the sky and over every living creature.
that moves on the ground..
We have dog owners in our crowd and cat owners..
These animals are now used to living inside our homes..
Our food and our clothing come from cattle, from sheep, from domesticated pigs..
Going even further than animals, the very land on which you now, I guess you are not.
standing, you are sitting, it's been shaped by mankind..
You live in Chicago, we're here in Chicago, and this place actually used to be a swamp..
And yet, even with all this accomplishment and ability, no human being can tame the tongue..

$^{201}$It says so right there..
No human being can tame the tongue..
While the things that inhabit this earth can be tamed, the tongue cannot be tamed by man..
This is terrible and sobering news..
Instead of us controlling our tongues, our tongues control us..
Our tongues don't just direct us towards evil..
They are themselves a restless force of evil that continuously fights to corrupt every.
part of us..
They're like a poison that infects everything we do and everyone we interact with..
And this, this is wrong..
James makes it clear to you and me that this is not right at all..
The entire letter of James reminds us that those who are believers in Jesus Christ are.
not people of death, but people of life, living children of God with a living faith who are.
called to be both hearers and doers of the word of God..
In verse 9, in verse 9, we are presented with this reality of what comes out of the mouth.
of men..
With the tongue, we praise our Lord and Father..
With the tongue, we curse human beings who have been made in God's likeness..
These are contrary actions..
Praises and curses strive towards separate purposes..
And not only this, the curses are directed at those made in God's likeness..
We are people who are in the image of God, a faint reflection of the one with infinite.
worth who is worthy of all praise..
So curses against these human beings made in God's likeness slander the very God who.
was just being praised..
And these come out of the same mouth, the mouth of those supposed living children of.
God with living faith..
This should not be..
James, in his usual fashion, asks rhetorical questions again..
If you would look with me to verses 11 and 12..
Can both fresh water and salt water flow from the same spring?.
My brothers and sisters, can a fig tree bear olives or a grapevine bear figs?.
Can both fresh water and salt water flow from the same spring?.
The implied and obvious answer is what?.
No, obviously not..
One when drank will satisfy thirst, the other will deepen thirst..
These are different waters..
They are not the same..
Can a fig tree bear olives or a grapevine bear figs?.
Again, the answer is no, right?.

$^{241}$These are not things that can happen..
To borrow a line from one of my classmates, we are proved through what we produce..
Fig trees being fig trees bear figs and olive trees bear olives..
They are not the same plant, the same with a grapevine..
Grapevines produce grapes because they are grapevines..
They bear their corresponding fruit..
So why are praise and cursing both flowing from the same source?.
How can both death and life be produced by the same tongue?.
What does that prove about the one who is speaking?.
James makes this clear to you and to me, that this is wrong..
It should not be and it must not be any longer..
You and I, being people who follow the Lord Jesus Christ, who profess faith in Jesus,.
must become living children of God with living faith..
Words of evil and death have no place coming from such people..
So then, knowing that the tongue holds a key place in the direction of our living, that.
our tongues direct us towards evil and that children of God should not be guided by or.
speak evil, what should you do?.
Is the solution to work hard to control our tongues?.
Is it to, from this point on, having heard what you heard, put all your effort into gaining.
control over our words?.
Obviously not..
If you look back at verse 8, no human power can tame the tongue..
It doesn't matter how much effort you put in..
You cannot force fresh water to flow out of a saltwater spring..
So what's the solution then?.
Do you want to be a person who is wise, complete, and whole?.
A person that is directed by righteousness rather than an evil tongue?.
If that is the case, then position yourself..
Position yourself to be shaped and led by the words of God rather than the words of.
men..
Because it is not a word of life that comes out of you that transforms you..
It is words of life that are given to you that transform you..
And God has given you his word to transform you..
James himself pulls from wisdom literatures such as Psalms and Proverbs..
And here is an example..
Never mind..
Where is it?.
One second..
Okay, guess it's not there..
If you have your Bibles with me, you can turn to Psalms..

$^{281}$The book of Psalms, its first chapter..
You'll be looking at verses one to three real briefly..
It is not on the screen, and that's okay..
I'll read it out for you, all right?.
Psalm chapter one, verses one to three..
Blessed is the one who does not walk in step with the wicked, or stand in the way that.
sinners take, or sit in the company of mockers, but whose delight is in the law of the Lord.
and who meditates on his law day and night..
That person is like a tree planted by streams of water, which yields its fruit in season,.
and whose leaf does not wither..
Whatever they do, prospers..
That's the example I give to you..
If you look at this verse, you'll find that there's this person here that's mentioned..
A person who resists evil and flourishes like a tree planted by streams of water..
And they do so by meditating on the word of God day and night..
Do you know what it means to meditate?.
It's not this concept of clearing your mind that we so often think about..
You're not emptying..
You are filling your mind..
In scripture, to meditate is to mutter, to murmur to yourself, and to speak the word.
of God as you read it over and over..
It's not just a mental effort either..
It's this engaging of your entire person, an exercise of your lips, your tongue, and.
your teeth..
To meditate is to engage fully and to truly take in the word of God..
This person here who is described, the one who is blessed, who does not walk in the ways.
of sin, is not directed by evil, and instead meditates on God's law day and night..
This is Jesus..
Meditate on God's word just as Jesus does..
And this is not new..
All right?.
This is not new at all..
This is the same truth over and over in the letter of James..
Our actions and behaviors are not the reason for our faith..
They are the result of our faith..
In this chapter that we have just looked at, chapter three, James calls for believers to.
correctly display the state of their hearts through what they say..
And so, having heard all of this, having seen the importance of the tongue in shaping the.
way in which you live, while also knowing that this is a daunting fight, one that you.
cannot win on your own, allow the word of God to direct the way in which you speak..

$^{321}$Be diligent..
Be a diligent hearer of the word of God so that you become a diligent doer of the word.
of God..
And by doing so, do not prove a bitter and critical heart through bitter and critical.
words..
Instead, prove to be a living child of God with a living faith through living words..
Let me close us in a brief word of prayer..
Would you bow your heads with me as we pray?.
Father, you are the one who gives life..
You are the breath in our lungs..
You are the one who spoke first and created all of creation..
And so, Lord, I ask in this moment that you would speak to your people, that you would.
speak to my brothers and sisters, that your word would be the first thing upon their heart,.
the thing that shapes them, because it is your righteousness that we cling to, your.
work that we cling to..
And so I ask that you would continue to place your hand upon them, that you would remove.
the calluses from their heart, that you would give their ears the ability to hear your word,.
their eyes the ability to see your word..
Lord, would you place your spirit in them anew that they might come to know you in deeper.
and deeper ways..
We pray all this in Jesus' name, amen..

$^{1}$Hi everyone, good to be back..
I was here last week and I think I spoke for about 25 minutes..
So today I'll speak within range again..
Last week I talked about storytelling and for those of you who weren't here, I talk.
about stories because I'm a children's book author and I'm also an artist and an educator..
So stories have a lot of meaning to me personally and I use a lot of stories in my work..
Today we'll be talking about the power of analogy and we're looking at Matthew chapter.
13 verses 24 to 30..
But before we kind of get into it, you'll see the subtitle says "Weed, Wheat or What?".
You're like, "What is that about?".
So before we get into it, let's recap a little about what happened last week..
If you were there, this is a nice reminder..
If you were not, then you got the cliff notes..
So number one, Jesus is the goat..
So he's the greatest of all time storyteller..
And last week we looked at the parable of the lost sheep, both in Luke and in Matthew..
So we looked at the two of them because even though they're the same story about the parable.
of the lost sheep, the way Jesus told it is different, which is why he's the goat..
Because he changes it based on the audience..
Who's watching and who are they?.
Are they the Pharisees and the religious leaders like in Luke?.
Or are they his own disciples like in Matthew?.
A great storyteller also changes the way he or she tells a story based on the context..
So what is happening around them?.
How are they gathering?.
So is it a public setting or is it a private setting?.
And that changes the tone and the voice of what the storyteller says..

from Old Testament to New Testament,.
what is going on here..

to the Israelites, to the Old Testament people..

and to enjoy the land all because of God's grace..

and the people are to be faithful..

the principles lay out in the Old Testament,.
especially the first five books, how to manage their land..

to the Old Testament people,.
it is not saying, okay, anything goes..

and you can just go in and do whatever you want, right?.

that he's gonna get this very lucrative job,.
and that he's gonna make up to \$10 million,.
and when he does, that's when he's gonna retire early.
and then start serving the Lord..
He thought that it was appropriate to wait.
and allocate time later on in his life to serve the Lord,.
and there was no immediacy,.
and there was no need to start his race anytime soon..
You know, this reminds me of the passage.
in James chapter four, 13 to 15, where James says,.
"Now listen, you who say today or tomorrow.
"we will go to this or that city,.
"spend a year there, carry on business, and make money..
"Why?.
"You don't even know what will happen tomorrow..
"What is your life?.
"You are a mist that appears for a little while.
"and then vanishes..
"Instead, you ought to say, if it is the Lord's will,.
"we will live and do this or that.".

$^{561}$In contrast to the MBA student,.
one of my inspirations is Dr. Stuart Wu..
I don't know if some of you might know him,.
but he's probably one of the most dedicated.
and faithful servants I've ever met in my life..
And I first encountered Dr. Wu.
when I was doing a short-term medical mission.
in Zhongshan, China..
He's a retired surgeon, and he would regularly,.
more than once a year, go out to remote parts of China.
where we would have to track mountainous areas.
to get to people and provide them medical care.
and also to share the gospel..
He did this into his late 80s,.
until he was 87 and then passed away..
And he never made a complaint that I knew of.
when he did this..
And so, I was less than half his age..
I was probably a third of his age when I first met him..
And I didn't have nearly as much stamina.
and as much zeal as he did..
And I wish to be like him,.
because he kind of constantly had this mindset.
of finishing the race and finishing well,.
even until his late 80s..
Nope, that's not it..
I know this last slide says active rest,.
but actually, my focus pivoted toward.
making sure that we have guardrails..
As we run the race and start doing God's work.
to spread his good news and make disciples,.
we need to make sure that we don't take.
an end justifies the means approach..
And that how we behave in the process.
of reaching that goal matters as much.
as actually reaching that goal..
So, even if there are great results.
of people coming to the church, of the church growing,.
it doesn't give you a pass on how you act.
in the way getting there..

$^{601}$The Lord cares as much about that journey.
as he does about the end goal that you're striving for..
You know, the last part of this passage,.
Paul emphasizes that he makes sure.
that he's not disqualified in his attempt.
to obtain the prize by making sure.
that he keeps his body in check..
In verse 27, he says, "No, I strike a blow to my body.
"and make it my slave, so that after I preach to others,.
"I myself will not be disqualified for the prize.".
I believe that he's actually alluding.
to keeping material and physical temptations at bay..
Because earlier in Corinthians,.
he had addressed the audience to flee.
from sexual immorality in chapter six..
And I think that he's alluding to this.
when he's talking about making sure.
that he's not disqualified..
He makes sure that as he's fulfilling the work of God,.
that he's not discredited and doesn't discredit.
the Lord's work by his behavior..
Sadly, in recent years, we've seen a lot of church leaders,.
even in our region, fall to sexual sin..
And this has had severe impact on the churches themselves,.
as well as people coming to the church..
And this is what we want to stay away from..
And it may not be such a blatant sin as sexual immorality..
It could be an arrogant attitude..
It could be poor financial stewardship..
It could be a lack of empathy for the people.
that we're actually trying to target..
In my devotions recently,.
I'm now finishing the book of Deuteronomy..
At the end of Deuteronomy,.
Moses is getting ready to go up to Mount Nebo and to die..
And he will never be able to cross into the promised land..
He gets a view of the promised land,.
but he's not allowed to cross it..
And this happened because he actually.
did not follow God's exact orders..

$^{641}$Even though he is a champion and a hero of the Bible,.
and he saved the Israelites from slavery,.
and took him into, or got him ready.
to go into the promised land,.
the Lord prevents him from going in,.
because instead of whispering to a rock.
to call forth water, he knocks it twice in anger..
And this was enough for the Lord.
to actually prevent him and penalize him.
from going into the promised land..
How we uphold ourselves during our work.
is as important as accomplishing the end result..
It's not only about the end point, but how we get there..
Not just about the finish line,.
but how we run the race itself..
So, I ask all of you, do you even lift, bruh?.
If you have been diligently doing God's work,.
keep at it, and remember that we're in a continuous marathon.
that requires training, diligence, dedication..
But also, the point that I want to highlight,.
and said that I changed,.
was also to make sure that we rest..
We, I think, especially as immigrants,.
or children of immigrants,.
there's this very strong work ethic that we develop..
And sometimes we bring that also into our faith,.
and we don't rest..
And the Lord prescribed the Sabbath for us,.
so that we can make sure that we rest as well,.
and are recharged so we can run even stronger,.
and for God..
Continuously train yourselves,.
keep yourselves sharp and ready,.
and your muscles going, you know,.
reading the word, praying, being in fellowship,.
serving actively in your communities,.
and then keeping yourselves accountable.
while in fellowship with others..
And for those of you who are honest and say,.
no, I don't lift, now's the time to start,.

$^{681}$because there is, it's never too late to get started..
And it's important to begin when you know.
that God's calling you to his great commission..
So, go run the race, and do your part in God's great work,.
and get those muscles going, and well conditioned..
Let me end this in prayer..
Heavenly Father, thank you for this opportunity.
to preach your word, and to understand that our faith.
is one that is demonstrated through action..
And Paul uses the visual of running a race..
I pray that for each one of us,.
you help us to understand the areas in our lives.
where we need to be better conditioned,.
or to start conditioning, and to operate these muscles,.
these spiritual muscles, so that we can be ready.
for your work that you've called us to,.
to advance your kingdom, and to make disciples.
for your kingdom..
In your name we pray, amen..
- Amen..

in the future..

sometimes it seems mysterious..

what God is doing in Christ..

we acknowledge that we are so limited in our sight..

saving Jews and Gentiles alike,.

to see how amazing you are,.

"Because you have done this,.
"cursed are you above all livestock.
"and above all beasts of the field..

$^{521}$"On your belly you shall go,.
"and dust you shall eat all the days of your life,".
which is almost a metaphor,.
a picture of utter humiliation, lowliness, defeat..
"I will put enmity," which is conflict, warfare,.
violence, "between you and the woman.
"and between your offspring and her offspring..
"He shall bruise your head,.
"and you shall bruise his heel.".
So this is the curse that God gives to the serpent..
But even in this curse, we find a promise.
when God says, interestingly,.
"I will put enmity between you and the woman,.
"between your offspring and her offspring..
"He shall bruise your head.".
There's a pronoun there of an offspring of the woman..
"He shall bruise your head,.
"and you shall bruise his heel.".
And so I wanna talk a little bit about that last part..
He shall bruise your head, you shall bruise his heel..
It's referring to the offspring or the seed of the woman..
In Hebrew, this is the word zara..
Its meaning is like an offspring, a descendant,.
a child, a literal seed..
And in the Bible, when we see this word used in this way,.
it always refers to a man, the seed of Abraham,.
the seed of David..
But in this one instance,.
of all the places I could find in the Bible,.
the seed describes a woman..
And this is because the seed is in,.
and it comes from the man..
It doesn't come from the woman..
So it's curious that God would talk.
about the seed of a woman..
This wouldn't really make sense normally,.
but I think this is significant..
Because in this promise,.
the seed of the woman is referring to a certain someone..
And if you can think of who it is,.

$^{561}$go ahead and just shout it out..
Exactly, exactly..
'Cause there's one person, one child,.
in all of human history,.
who was born without a human father..
So literally, Jesus, the Messiah,.
born of the Virgin Mary,.
could only be the seed of a woman..
Jesus Christ, the Son of God,.
the seed of the woman,.
promised by God from the very beginning.
that he would be the one to bruise,.
to crush the head of the serpent..
God says, "He will bruise your head,.
"you will bruise his heel.".
And so you can compare the two..
To bruise someone's heel,.
it's like a snake bite to the back..
You don't see it coming..
It's kind of an underhanded, deceptive attack..
But if a serpent were to come on the stage,.
and I don't know if we have snakes in Chicago..
I know we have rats..
Maybe if we had some more snakes, we'd have less rats..
But if a snake came on stage and bit me in the heel,.
it would hurt, it would not be great,.
but it wouldn't kill me..
It's not a fatal blow..
But if I turned around and stomped on that snake's head,.
that's it..
It's a fatal blow..
It's a death strike..
A complete defeat for that snake..
And so in that curse, there's also a promise.
that this one figure, this male offspring of the woman,.
this savior, would be bruised on the heel,.
would suffer some temporary defeat..
But in that defeat, he would ultimately defeat the serpent..
And so this passage right here is known.
as the Proto-Evangelium, which just means the first gospel..

$^{601}$It is the first gospel message in all of the Bible..
The first glimpse of hope, promise of redemption,.
fulfilled in Jesus Christ's death and resurrection..
Because in death, Jesus was rejected and scorned.
by his own people, betrayed by them..
Betrayed even by a disciple who he loved as a brother..
On the way to the cross, he was abandoned.
by the rest of his disciples..
In that crucifixion, in that rejection and abandonment,.
Jesus suffered the serpent's bite to the heel..
Yet in his resurrection, he crushed the head of the serpent.
declaring victory over sin, death, and the grave..
And so this was the hope, this savior figure to come,.
was the hope of Adam and Eve, that one of their descendants.
would one day crush the head of the serpent..
That this figure, this messiah, the savior,.
would defeat Satan and rid humanity.
of his evil schemes once and for all..
It is this savior who is the messiah of Israel,.
the one in which the people of Israel.
hoped in for thousands of years..
The one whose birth we celebrate every year at Christmas..
He is the one upon which all of our hopes rest..
All of God's people rest their hope in this one savior..
He is the solution to all of our problems..
The ones that, the sin problem that has plagued.
all of mankind throughout history and plagues us today..
Our problem is sin, it's devastating effects on our bodies,.
our families, every aspect of our life is marred by sin..
But just as it is written, she will give birth to a son.
and you shall call his name Jesus..
For he will save his people from their sins..
This is the hope that we must cling on to..
The same hope that Adam and Eve, even after the fall,.
even after such a devastating loss of perfection,.
this was the hope they held to..
The same hope we see throughout the scriptures..
So many of God's faithful held on to this hope.
of a savior, of a redeemer..
One example I wanna look at from the book of Job..

$^{641}$A great example, Job was a man who lost nearly everything,.
who by worldly standards had nothing to live for..
His possessions, gone, his children, dead,.
his own friends accused him of evil..
His wife even asked him, you know,.
why don't you just curse God and die already?.
Yet in spite of all his suffering and anguish,.
Job could confidently declare this..
I know that my redeemer lives and that in the end,.
he will stand on the earth..
And after my skin has been destroyed,.
yet in my flesh, I will see God..
I myself will see him with my own eyes,.
I and not another, how my heart yearns within me..
You see, despite Job's sorrow and suffering,.
he was able to hold on to hope in God, his redeemer..
And so I ask, can you, can we say with Job,.
I know my redeemer lives in the midst of our suffering,.
my redeemer lives..
In the midst of frustration, difficulty,.
disappointment with family, with friends,.
my redeemer lives..
In the midst of pain and anguish, physical ailment,.
my redeemer lives..
When you lose a loved one, my redeemer lives..
You see, that is our hope, that Jesus Christ,.
the seed of the woman, he lives, he's our hope..
It's this very same hope,.
which has been held onto for millennia..
The prophets all wrote of it, they spoke of this hope..
Many people have waited for thousands of years.
for this hope..
Now we have him, we have this hope..
Yet unlike all the people of God that came before us,.
we don't have to wait and look forward to it..
We look back to something that already happened..
We know what happened, we have a confidence of it,.
of the time that Jesus entered the world.
to live a perfectly righteous life that we never could..
To suffer and die a painful, humiliating death.

$^{681}$that we never would..
To bear the wrath of God that we deserved..
To defeat sin, to defeat Satan..
And we know that not only was he born in this world.
of the Virgin Mary, not only did he suffer.
and die under Pontius Pilate,.
not only was he buried dead for three days.
after three days, he rose again to life..
And so we can say confidently, as Job said,.
I know my Redeemer lives..
Not only is this a present reality that we look back to,.
that we commemorate yearly,.
we also have an even greater future hope that we hold onto..
The second advent, the second coming of Jesus Christ.
into the world, the Messiah who will once and for all.
defeat the serpent..
And when he comes back, he will raise all his believers.
who have fallen, he will raise us and give us a new body,.
uncorrupted by sin, new minds, unstained by evil..
He will put the enemy under his feet.
and then put an end to sin and death and pain for all time..
And he will give us eternity with God in a new heavens,.
new earth, a new place of perfection..
And this is our joy, this is our peace, this is our hope..
This is our solution to the problem of sin, shame and guilt,.
loneliness, hopelessness, depression, sickness,.
death, frustration, trouble, trial, tribulation..
Jesus Christ is our hope..
So during this Christmas season, we should be encouraged,.
encouraged by this hope of who he is, what he has done.
and what he will ultimately accomplish..
Even in the midst of difficulties and troubles,.
we have a hope, we have something to hold onto.
that will keep us going..
And therefore we should be encouraged.
and we should encourage one another..
Look to a brother or sister,.
if you see someone around you, reach out..
If they're struggling, so many of us are,.
offer them that same hope, remind them,.

$^{721}$encourage them with this hope..
It's not just a hope that we have, we share with one another..
There's a passage I wanna, I'll just mention it,.
I won't read it, but Ephesians chapter two, verse 12,.
Paul is reminding the brothers and sisters in Ephesus.
of the time before they were in Christ,.
when they were alienated from the household of God,.
they were strangers and in the world they had no hope..
They were without God..
And there's people like that today..
And we once were like that with no hope in the world,.
with no ultimate solution or answer to all the troubles.
and pains of this world..
But in Christ, we have that hope..
And it's not just enough for us to hold onto the hope.
or to share it with our brothers and sisters,.
but we have to reach out to those in the world.
who are lost, stumbling in darkness, who don't have hope..
Share that message of hope with them..
I think Christmas time is a perfect time.
because it's already on everyone's mind..
There's gonna be family meals,.
you might be sitting next to somebody in your own family.
who is lost and without hope..
Share that hope with them, a coworker, a friend,.
a stranger on the bus or the train or whatever,.
share that hope with them..
It's the perfect time..
We have the hope that the world needs..
So as we approach our celebration of Christmas,.
of the advent of Messiah, Emmanuel, God with us,.
who as we heard earlier is the wonderful counselor,.
almighty God, everlasting father and prince of peace,.
the seed of the woman and the savior of mankind,.
let us draw close to him, hold onto him, find hope in him,.
and be as willing and as eager to share that hope.
with someone else..
And so my prayer for all of us, for you guys,.
is the same as Paul's prayer for the Romans,.
when he says, "May the God of hope fill you.

$^{761}$"with all joy and peace in believing,.
"so that by the power of the Holy Spirit,.
"you may abound in hope.".
Let's pray..
Heavenly Father, Lord God almighty, I thank you, Lord..
We love you, we praise your precious and holy name..
We thank you that even in the midst of a dark,.
sin-stained world full of evil and trouble and suffering,.
you have given forth a light in the midst of darkness,.
a light that we look to, a light that we have,.
that we hold onto, and God, I thank you for this light..
I thank you for your love that we see in Jesus Christ..
Help us, God, to be encouraged by this hope..
Help us to be strengthened and matured in our faith.
by this hope, and to be so filled with love.
for you and others that we take this hope to the world,.
who needs it more than anything, God..
So that is my prayer today, that we would all be,.
not just hearers of your word, but doers who act,.
who take this message and apply it to our lives, God..
Help us in this, I pray, for the glory.
and in the name of our Lord, Jesus Christ, amen..

how God does things..

he'll be with us..

what are you gonna do?.

"At the time of the offering,".
and so the bowels and all prophets bowed,.

"and the wood and the stones and the dust.
"and licked up the water that was in the trench..
"Are you praying that God will show up in your life?".
Elijah prayed and asked the Lord,.
"Let it be known this day that you are God in Israel.
"and that I am your servant..
"I need you to show up..
"Are you praying that God will show up in your life?".
Now, here's one thing, God is always at work in your life..
God is always present in your life..

is that we're praying that God show up in our life..
Make it known..
Show us that you're real..

$^{721}$because you know what, we need to be reminded..

the discouragement, the things that we face.
each and every single day..

we're gonna need strength..

we're gonna need some encouragement along the way..

all my illustrations have been on death and struggles,.
but here's one more of an email.
that I actually received this week that actually struck me..

for a while, he says,.

with migraines, with Crohn's disease, with all of that..

by the time you get this..

$^{561}$I have called you by name, and you are mine..
You belong to me..
No longer you belong to the oppressor,.
or your previous political power,.
or anyone that has a hold on you,.
or anything that has hold on you..
Whether it's the shame, guilt, depression,.
all those things no longer have any hold on you.
because you don't belong to them..

God knows you by name and call you by name.
because you are his..
And he said, "You are mine.".
God know us, thank God, right?.
We belong to the new king, Jesus Christ,.
who died on the cross for our sin,.
to set us free from any oppressive powers,.
ultimately sin and darkness and death..
And Jesus free us and give us this new life, right?.
And Mary Magdalene experienced it,.
and we should too, we should too..
Now, before we close in prayer,.
we would close today's service with a communion..
I think we have the communion elements ready..
And by doing that,.
we proclaim to the world,.
as we protect the bread and the cup..
Remember, this is the Passover meal.
Jesus set up for generations of Christians, right?.
The Passover story, find fulfillment in Jesus.
because Jesus is the lamb of God..
He set us free, right?.
He set us free and we belong to him..

we know we belong to Jesus and to him alone..
Let's do that because of grace of God,.
then we can be called the children.
of the kingdom of the light..
Let's all pray..
Father, as we bow our heads to pray to you,.

$^{601}$we know we belong to you..
And thank you for being our king,.
being our Lord..
You have called us by name and we are yours..
Thank you for loving us so amazingly and so unconditionally..
As we see the cross,.
as we see Jesus hung on the cross because of our sin,.
in order to love us and to redeem us and ransom us.
from all kinds of powers on the earth,.
sin and darkness and death,.
they no longer have any holes in our lives..
Thank you for the change that you brought about.
in your grace..
It's not because of what we have done,.
but because of what your son has done for all of us..
So as we observe the communion together,.
taking the bread and the cup,.
bring us back to your table..
Bring us back to your table of grace,.
knowing that we can partake in eternity.
because of your sheer grace..
Thank you, Jesus..
In Christ's name, we pray..

$^{241}$and the Israelite places are many in the midst of the land..

which leads us to the next point..
Because when things--when we get discouraged--.
I love what Tim Keller says on this one..

God uses the story in Elijah where he encounters both the angel--.
an angel--and the Lord..

He allows him to sleep..

"Arise, get up, and eat.".

touch, all of those things,.

because we are physical beings in a physical world..

he ministers to us mentally, emotionally..

wait, are you the one who's supposed to come,.

After all, in verse 15, "And the Lord said to him,.

you shall anoint to be prophet in your place..

the Tishbit of Tishbe in Gilead,.

$^{1}$早晨各位,這兩個星期我都在Chicago,所以今天我們暫停Mark Sir的港島系列Chosen,不用失望,下個星期會繼續,到時記得準時出席,今天大家稍安勿躁,先聽我分享..
今年我用Timothy Keller和他太太選寫的每日心言去靈修,每日只有一版,不是很長,.
久不久有一兩版或一兩節經文對我特別深刻或很有趣,那幾天我會想起靈修篇章的心言.話說有日我和我老公出去食飯,.
最近一次,我經常笑我老公有選擇困難症,因為無論每次我們出去食飯,去那間餐館去過多少次都好,.
他會望著餐牌,要用很長時間去研究餐單,無論裡面有多少選擇也好,餐館內去過多少次也好,他都要用很多時間,很多掙扎才可以下單..
不單止這樣,還要食一食,通常他會說早知不要點這個,其實我應該點那個好些,因為那個似乎多些食物,.
抵食些,甚至有剩餘的可以帶回家,但價錢差不多.今次和他食飯,這件事當然是歷史重演,.
我突然間腦海裡面出現一句最近我靈修時的經文,在《箴言》26章11節,.
他說:如未人一再做蠢事,如同狗轉身吃自己吐出來的東西.我和我老公說:Daddy,《箴言》裡面有這句經文,.
在你這個情況下,是否蠢人一再做蠢事,如同狗轉身吃自己吐出來的東西..
我老公看著我,扁嘴,低頭,《箴言》真是句句精金.今天講到的主題,用盡一生的腦袋,經文出自《箴言》1章1至7節,.
我們先低頭祈禱.親愛的主,我們一生,願也都尊你的名為聖,願你的國降臨,.
願你的旨意行在地上,如同行在天上,你祝福我們用心靈和誠實去敬拜你,虛心聆聽你話語的人..
我先跟大家讀一讀這個《箴言》1章1至7節..
大衛的兒子以色列王所羅門的箴言,要使人懂得智慧和憤悔,明白通達的言語,使人領受明智的憤悔..
就是公義,公平和正直,使愚民靈巧,使年輕人有知識,有智慧,智謀..
智慧人聽見,增長學問,聰明人得著智謀,明白箴言和曉悅,懂得智慧人的言辭和謎語,敬威耶和華是智識的開端..
如往人藐視智慧和憤悔..
箴言1章1開始,所羅門就解釋箴言的目的,是要讓讀者去研讀,去思考箴言,從中得著智慧去生活..
人的一生有很多起起跌跌,充滿了難以預料的事情..
你有錢或沒有錢也好,煩惱自然會找上門..
面對每天的挑戰,箴言所提供的智慧,幫助人有洞察的能力和理解能力去辨別出,作出有智慧的選擇..
有知識不代表有智慧,因為知識只是在說對事實的認知,智慧是將所知道的,所認識的運用出來..
例如人可以明白金融系統的運作方式,智慧是在說你能夠利用這個金融系統的運作方式去管理金錢..
使人領受明智的憤悔,就是公義,公平和正直..
能夠對事物有正確的概念,也有清澈明確的想法,讓我們有能力去辨別有智慧的教導..
我們聽了很多東西,但究竟哪些才是有智慧的教導呢?.
區別真偽,善惡,理解一些有智慧的說話..
有領悟,有判斷能力防範錯誤,並且將所學的應用,甚至幫助我們身邊的人..
菲勒比書一章十節,使你們能分辨是非..
使愚民靈巧,使年輕人有知識有智慧..
《箴言》十四章十五節,無知的人什麼話都信,通達人謹慎自己的腳步..
當然,智慧對我們所有人都很有用,我們都想擁有..
但特別對一些思想比較單純的人,就更加需要聽到多一些智慧的建議,能夠重組獲得益處..
幫助那個人思考,釐清真偽,避免做錯事..
當然更重要的是逃避誘惑,或者中了壞人的詭計..
像所羅門所說,壞人的外表可以很善良,但其實他們就像蛇一樣假惡..
青年時期是接收各種訊息的年紀,我們經常聽到年輕人就像一個海綿一樣,.
很容易吸收很多東西,他們心智未成熟,容易衝動,性急,很多時候想做就去做,容易受人唆擺,不考慮後果..
我想我們在座每一個人,要去想一想的時候,都會想起我們小時候做了多少蠢事..

$^{41}$現在的確是一個資訊的年代,不同的資訊其實是誰手可得,你只要有個電話,基本上你想知道什麼,你打進去,你就可以找到答案..
只不過你不知道這些資訊是從哪裡來的,對你有益還是有害,是真還是假,或者製造這些資訊的人,背後到底有什麼動機..
我讀神學院的時候學了一個很重要的功課,就是每一次當我們要引用一些文章,或者一些資料的時候,.
我們都需要探究清楚知道我們所引用,接收的訊息是從哪裡來的,是誰寫的呢,是真還是假的呢,.
不是每本書都是好書,不是所有資訊都是正確的..
今時今日我們看的新聞,其實都是要千挑萬選,因為有些新聞已經不是再用公正無私的態度,客觀的去報導新聞,.
只是淪落成為了國家的宣傳工具.還記不記得在2000年,香港有不少騙徒,宣稱有千年蟲的蛀蟲藥,.
有騙徒對千年蟲問題一知半解的市民去購買,以訛傳訛,你怕我又怕,.
有部分不熟悉電腦的市民就以為千年蟲好像一個瘟疫一樣,一個傳染病一樣的病毒,.
花了很多錢來買這些解藥,被人騙錢.上星期我才有個朋友跟我說了一個笑話,.
他說他在一套劇集裡面,其中一幕講到一條村裡面的村民衝著去教會信耶穌,.
因為教會門口有一塊牌寫著信耶穌得水牛,.
個個信以為真,走了去教會等牧師派水牛,.
但其實教會門口那塊牌是日久失修,永生這兩個字少了一點,同一畫,.
雖然聽起來很好笑,是一個笑話,但想想如果真的發生好像不太奇怪,.
智慧人聽見增長學問,聰明人得著自謀,明白真言和巧語,懂得智慧人的言辭和謎語..
說開又說,你身邊有沒有一些你信得過的弟兄姊妹,.
能夠在你的生命裡面,你的生活裡面面對一些困難,或者一些你掌握不到的事上,.
能夠跟你聊天,能夠跟你一起分析,給你意見,跟你一起祈禱呢?.
忘記多少歲開始,我發覺自己想事情不是很全面,我是一個過分樂觀的人,.
由那時候開始,我很喜歡找一些認識我,跟我很親密的弟兄姊妹一起分享,去問他們意見,.
慢慢這個動作就成為了我的習慣,多年來,加加減減,今時今日我存了一班弟兄姊妹在我身邊,.
在不同的事情上,我都可以跟他們一起分享,有時這件事我去問A,那件事B比較厲害,我會找B去分享..
這班跟我一起追求成長的智囊團,陪伴了我很多年,跟我一起成長,看著我掙扎,支持我,.
在需要的時候跟我一起祈禱,跟我一起仰望神,同樣我都是他們的智囊團..
《箴言一章五節》這裡,正正就是在說我們人願意謙卑聆聽,尋求意見是多麼重要,不是靠我們自己..
更加重要當然是我們找一些比較淑齡的弟兄姊妹,有追求心的弟兄姊妹一起去分享,一起去成長..
願意聽意見受教的人,在《箴言》這裡,就是在說他們是一些有智慧的人,.
懂得找適當的人去尋求意見,可以對事情有更透徹的了解..
說起問問題,說起來我們基督徒很喜歡問神的心意,神的旨意,.
我們很希望當我們問的時候,神有一個很清澈的答案給我們,最好就幫我選好,不用我煩..
其實什麼是神的心意,什麼是神的旨意?.
如果你經常問這個問題的時候,特別是在你遇到困難,想神幫你選的時候,其實這個問題是問錯了的..
因為神的心意,神的旨意不是一個功能,不是用來幫人解決問題,化解疑惑..
如果你是真心想知道什麼是神的心意,神的旨意的時候,其實答案就在聖經裡面..
在聖經裡面,神已經很清清楚楚地告訴我們他的心意,他的旨意..
例如約翰福音13章34節,這裡說你們要彼此相愛..
亞馬太福音6章33節,要先求他的國和他的兒..
約翰一書2章15節,不要愛世界和世界上的東西,若有人愛世界,愛父的心就不在他裡面了.等等..
這些就是神的心意,這些就是神的旨意..

$^{81}$在聖經裡面清楚列明,可能不是人想找到的答案,甚至可能聽過很多次,你沒有什麼特別感覺..
要先求他的國和他的兒,這些東西都要加給你們..
是一個命令,也是一個應許..
如果你花點時間去消化這節經文,其實我們做基督徒是很有福氣的..
我們先追求神的兒和神的國,其他東西是自然神就給你的,你不需要擔心,你不需要去求..
經威耶和華是知識的開端,如往人藐視智慧和憤悔..
真言裡面不單止一章七節提到經威耶和華是知識的開端,.
真言九章十節,經威耶和華是智慧的開端,認識自聖者便是聰明..
上年我去伊拉克短孫的時候,我認識了一位姐妹,她在香港美國的英特爾工作了27年,她越做越高級..
經常會坐公司的飛機到處去工作,逢星期一就飛,星期四晚上就會回到家..
每個星期都如是,因為她經常不在家,她的女兒長期不開心,因為一會兒要去公公婆婆家住,一會兒又奶奶爺爺,一會兒可能會去另外一些人家..
她的工作很繁重,壓力很大,她說當她的同輩,她的同事升職快過她,那個壓力會更加大,會令她懷疑自己的能力..
單親媽媽做公養家,照顧女兒,處理家裡的事,她結果捱到身體出現毛病..
當她病得快要死的時候,她突然開始在想,我是不是快要死了?.
如果我突然死了怎麼辦?她在想,其實我不認識神,我雖然是一個基督徒,但我不太認識神,我不太認識耶穌..
她一想到如果我死了之後上天堂,見到神,三不識七,還要24/7天天對著祂..
她說再想想,還要永遠,她說想起我會很害怕,我不想和一個陌生人長期對著,她說實在很難想像..
因為那場大病,她重新檢視生命,後來她康復了,她決定要滴起心肝去認識給她生命的主..
沒多久公司有個不錯的機會,她乘機把握機會提早退休..
今時今日她已經退休了八年,她過著一些很簡樸,很簡單的生活..
一個星期有兩天去參加Bible Study Fellowship,查經團契裡面去查經和服侍,教會有需要的時候去教會幫忙..
和她聊天的時候,我覺得有很大的得著,我很欣賞她,覺得她很有智慧..
我也想起她是一個很謙卑的人,我和她去短孫的時候,她做的崗位其實是很卑微的,其實她是全部都懂的..
做她的頭的那個,反而沒有她那麼懂事,但是她從來沒有說過一句話,令你覺得她很厲害..
她也沒有挑戰給她工作的那位姐妹,有些事情可能可以做得更加好..
她跟我說她很感恩有這場大病,令她醒過來,她多了很多時間可以在家陪她女兒,也可以參加查經班去認識神..
在人的眼中,她當然有一份很令人羨慕的工作,賺很多錢,她住在一個很貴的社區裡面..
但是她沒有留戀這些東西,她也沒有留戀以前花錢買東西,她從來不需要想,不用看價錢,不需要再去找更豐厚的人工升職..
生命裡面的人和事,好像重新排位過,因為她現在很清楚知道在她生命裡面,什麼是最重要..
《箴言》二十四章三至四節,房屋因智慧建造,因聰明立穩,又因知識屋內充滿各樣美好寶貴的財物..
詩篇一百二十七篇一至二節,若不是耶和華建造房屋,建造的人就枉然勞力.若不是耶和華看守城池,看守的人就枉然警醒..
你們清晨早起,夜晚安歇,吃奴奴得來的飯本是枉然,唯有耶和華所親愛的必叫他安然睡覺..
若不是耶和華建造,建造的人枉然勞力.早上起床,夜晚休息,吃奴奴得來的飯本是枉然..
願望人藐視智慧和憤悔,《箴言》一章七節提醒,基本上只有傻瓜才會用我們一生的腦袋去建立我們眼前或今世以為能滿足,能給我們幸福安穩的生活..
卻輕視從神而來的智慧和憤悔,有屬靈遠大的眼光去鋪排永恆的生命..
2023年接二連三,我們家裡也收到很多沉重的消息,其中六月的時候,我小時候的偶像和我很親近的小表姐離開人世..
由她覺得不舒服入醫院,兩個星期後確診肺癌末期,再不夠兩個星期她就離開了世界..
她入院之後,我很多時候都會跟她互傳短訊,因為我知道她每天晚上都睡在病床上,特別是在日本凌晨的時分,.
我知道她白天眼睛都不見,所以我特別多跟她聊天..
如果那天我出門,我會拍一些照片給她看,因為有些地方是我們小時候一起去過的,我們一起懷緬過去..

$^{121}$她離開了芝加哥差不多三十年,當中只回來過幾次,所以有很多地方都不同了,有些新的東西,我又會拍照給她看,跟她介紹一下..
她住在醫院的時候,她跟我說,很諷刺,就像Katrina那樣說,她說我一直在減肥,有一個目標的磅數,她說進來之後瘦了幾磅,.
我現在的磅數就是我一直夢寐以求的.我們又會說回我們小時候,以前我去找她,在華富村一起玩,一起出街的時候,.
剛開始移民的時候,我們兩位表姊妹住在同一個房間,很想念香港,我們兩個一起哭了一個月,甚至很多年後,我去日本探望她,跟她傳福音,我們談到死亡的問題..
每天如是,傳著傳著的短訊,有一天她突然開始沒有回覆,一天沒有回覆,兩天沒有回覆,第三天我的大表姐告訴我,她已經離開了這個世界..
她入院之前一點舒服,一點不舒服都沒有,還安排了一家人準備去旅行.12月初回香港之前,我們收到一個消息,我們的伴郎在香港入了醫院..
回到香港之前,我們有點擔心,不單單是擔心他,其實我們在想,不知道香港的醫院情況如何,我們回到香港之後,有沒有可能去探望他呢?.
他12月底生日,我丈夫當時希望回到香港的時候,沒有多久出院,我們可以跟他一起慶祝生日.結果我們還沒有上機,他已經離開了..
消息來得很突然,我們基本上好像完全消化不了,回到香港,結果我們在他生日那一天,去參加他家人為他舉辦的追思會..
2023年終於過去,回到香港之後,回到美國,其實我一直都很忙.2月稍為回復正常的時候,有一天坐在客廳,我丈夫問我,.
媽媽,去年發生了那麼多事,又有幾個跟我們那麼親密的人離開了,其實對你有什麼影響?你猜我怎麼回答他?.
這一分鐘好好的,還在計劃去旅行,突然之間不舒服進了醫院,不到一個月就離開了,大家都還沒有消化到他病重,轉頭已經離開..
剛才說的那兩個人跟我年紀差不多,你問我對我有什麼影響?我在想的是,怎麼會沒有影響?.
有人可以每天做4分鐘的plank,40個掌上壓,少糖少鹽,少澱粉質,只是吃有機食物,早睡早起,不過分操勞,操練有好的EQ..
但你知不知道這樣做也好,其實也不保證你健健康康,長命百歲..
我有個朋友熬到五個兒子都終於出生了,他獎勵自己買了一輛Jaguar,搬到downtown,想著可以走路上班,.
結果車子落地不久就中風,左邊身體沒有活動能力,坐輪椅..
他太太結果把Jaguar換成了minivan,方便推他進去..
想想人生是不是真的就是這樣,好像傳道書那樣形容,一章二至三節說,虛空的虛空,虛空的虛空,全是虛空..
人一切的牢獄,就是他在日光之下的牢獄,有什麼益處呢?.
人的一生是不是就是這樣,是不是就是這麼恐怖,就是這麼虛空?.
我們窮一生的精力去計劃,去籌算我們的人生,去到這個年紀,可能有時還要想著,.
怎樣也不敢吃,那樣也不敢吃.我昨天才跟一個朋友說,他舅父年輕讀書的時候很窮,.
天天吃雞,只可以吃雞,到年紀大的時候身體不好,醫生叫他最好多吃點雞胸,.
因為這個人是醫生,到我已經有錢了,我什麼都可以吃的時候,結果還是天天吃雞..
我們看N這麼多篇的文章,聽N這麼多個朋友的意見,我們都是想確保我們的生活能夠有保障,.
我能夠安心,我能夠得到最好的資訊去幫助我去過一個平平穩穩,很安舒的人生..
但是我想你和我都知道,這個世界不是這樣的,當你的投資持續虧損,.
努力經營的得不到回報,突然病起來,生命倒數,死亡臨近的時候,.
所有你平時很緊張的東西,你看得很寶貴的東西,突然全部都沒有意思..
睡在床上的時候,無論你的戶口裡有多少錢,你衣櫃裡有多少漂亮的衣服,.
房子有多大多漂亮,我想起我自己,廚房裡有多少我看為很寶貴的沙煲冷炒,.
或者你在人面前有多麼的德高望重,誰在乎?.
用一生的腦袋去追求今世的款足,但有時我們甚至沒有好好經營我們和我們家人的關係,.
和教會弟兄姊妹的關係,有沒有想過病起來沒有人探你,很慘..
武漢重掌管生命創造你,給你生命的神,去問他,.
知取智慧,其實我應該怎樣去過我的一生,是先後次序的問題..
弟兄姊妹當你看到生命的無常,或者像吳牧師禱告提起有兩位姊妹昨天離開,.
像我這樣去年也有些和我們很親密的至親朋友離開,.
你看到人多麼無能為力失控的時候,你是否只懂得擔心,.

$^{161}$發財賣財去找一些方法去確保自己長命一點,不要生病,.
你是否很怕死,所以經常都憂憂愁愁,終日唉聲嘆氣..
其實死,我們每個人都有一死,走不掉的,.
Life is uncertain,但是Death is certain,問題不是我們想想要做些什麼不用死,.
因為死是必然的,但是會不會是需要多花時間去想想我們怎樣去過我們這一生,.
怎樣去預備我們自己去創造我們的做物主,.
我們一起低頭祈禱..
主啊求你引導我們的心思意念,.
教準我們的眼光,我們的心思,.
是在你裡面去尋求得著智慧,.
尋求你的引領,我們去怎樣面對生命,.
特別在我們生命遇到困難,病痛,挑戰的時候,.
拿開人的心思意念,就算我們突然想的時候也好,.
轉頭幾個second,你將我們的心思意念轉化到你裡面去想,去思考,.
在你的話語裡面去尋求,怎樣繼續前進,.
繼續怎樣去過我們的生活,.
看我們的生命,幫助我們每個人,.
怎樣去預備好我們自己,有一天我們要見你的面,.
都是無愧的,都是嚮往你與我們的同在,.
這樣去祈禱,奉耶穌得勝命求,.
如果你想的時候,可以在你的座位上,.
花一點時間祈禱,然後我們散會,.
祝福大家.

\section{18:21-35}
\label{sec:ON4fMvKp6vs}
\textbf{Forfeiting Forgiveness (Matthew 18\_21-35) - George Crawley}
\newline
\newline

$^{1}$All right, good morning, everybody..
Let's quickly pray with me..
Heavenly Father, I just pray now that you would use this time, use this word..
Let it not be a man's words, but let it be your word for your people and for your glory..
So I pray that you would speak through me, speak to each of our hearts, Father God, to.
make us more like the Lord Jesus Christ..
And I pray this in his name, amen..
So in December of 2003, a man named Gary Ridgway was sentenced by a Seattle judge to 48 life.
sentences..
In addition to this, he was sentenced 10 years for every one of those life sentences..
So he was facing 480-year sentence on top of 48 consecutive life sentences..
And it may seem extreme, but legally speaking, the sentence, this punishment was well-deserved.
because Gary Ridgway is more commonly known as the Green River Killer..
And he is the second most prolific serial killer in the history of the United States.
of America..
And while he was standing before the judge on trial for these 48 murders, he was stone-faced..
He had no emotion..
And he had actually confessed to killing over 70 women throughout Washington state, although.
he was only tried for 48 of them..
And through the entire sentencing process, he was stone-faced, he was emotionless..
And in the court proceedings, the judge had invited family members of these victims to.
come and speak before the court..
And so these families came up, and they bared their soul, they poured out their grief, their.
heartbreak, their rage towards this man who had taken everything from them—mothers,.
daughters, wives, sisters—all lost to this man who sat in the very same courtroom as.
them, absolutely remorseless..
And I got a few quotes here of some of the things that these families said, some mocking.
Gary Ridgway, some condemning this man for what he did to their families..
And so a few of the things that they said I have here..
"He's an animal..
I wish for him to have a long, suffering, cruel death.".
One woman said, "He's going to go to hell, and that's exactly where he belongs.".
Through all these statements and many more just like them, Ridgway remained emotionless..
But that is until one man took the podium, a father whose daughter had her life snatched.
away by this man..
And the father took the podium, and to everyone's surprise, this is what he said..
"Mr. Ridgway, there are people here that hate you..
I am not one of them..
You've made it difficult to live up to what I believe, and that is what God says to do,.
which is to forgive.".

$^{41}$And at that moment, the entire courtroom was stunned in silence as he said this next sentence..
"You are forgiven, sir.".
And at that, that shocking display of mercy and forgiveness, for the first time in months.
of court proceedings, Gary Ridgway broke down in tears, and he cried..
And there's a clip of this on YouTube..
If you look it up, you can search "The Power of Forgiveness, Gary Ridgway.".
And every time I watch that clip, I find it difficult not to myself tear up because it's.
just so powerful..
It's so full of emotion on display in the courtroom..
The heartbreak, the pain, the anger of those families who've just lost a piece of themselves,.
their desire for vengeance..
And then one man among many stands up and offers, extends forgiveness and mercy to a.
guilty murderer, a serial killer..
And when I see that, I feel a tug at my own heart, a tug of conviction, a conviction that.
asks me, "What would I do in that same position if it was my mother or my sister, my wife.
or my child?.
Would I be able to forgive like that?.
Could I forgive like that?.
Should I even forgive something so egregious, something so terrible?.
Does a murderer like that, does he deserve that forgiveness?.
How could that father have forgiven him?.
How could he do that?.
Why would he do that?".
And so today we'll be reading a portion of teachings from the Lord Jesus Christ that.
answers those very questions and it answers our questions when we find ourselves struggling.
to forgive, not wanting to forgive..
And so my passage I'll be reading from today is Matthew chapter 18, verses 21 through 35..
And before I get into the passage, I kind of want to explain and set up a little bit.
what is going on in the context of this teaching Jesus gives..
And so prior to this, Jesus had just taught his disciples his way of forgiveness, how.
when a brother or sister sins against them, how are they to respond?.
And what he tells them is when a brother or sister sins against you, you go to them and.
you tell them what they've done in hopes that they will repent and you will forgive them.
and you'll be restored, reconciled together..
But if they refuse to repent, you go and take two or three witnesses with you and together.
you'll go to this brother or sister who is in sin against you with the hope that you'll.
be restored and reconciled to them, that they will repent and you will forgive them..
But if they still refuse to repent, then you take the matter before the entire church with.
the hopes that the weight of the whole body of believers will cause this person to repent.
and then you forgive them and be reconciled and restored in brotherhood..

$^{81}$But if even then they repent, Jesus says to treat them, deal with them as a pagan, as.
a tax collector, as an outsider..
And so this is what Jesus is now responding to in this passage..
And after teaching these steps to his disciples, how they are to forgive a brother who sins.
against them, Peter comes up, he comes to the Lord and he asks him this question, "Lord,.
how often will my brother sin against me and I forgive him?.
As many as seven times?".
Which is a pretty good question Peter asks here, because if we're honest with ourselves.
we would probably have a similar question..
"Well, how many times Lord should I forgive?.
Yes, I know that you want me to forgive.".
And we generally agree that extending forgiveness is a good thing..
And we certainly know how good it feels to be forgiven..
But I think we all kind of think to ourselves, "There must be a limit, right?.
You don't expect me to forgive unconditionally if they keep hurting me or sinning against.
me..
My mercy, my patience, my forgiveness, it can only go so far..

$^{1}$Good morning family. It is great to be together again. Last week we finished up.
Matthew chapter 5 and so this week we're going to be beginning Matthew chapter 6..
And Jesus opens Matthew chapter 6 talking about hypocrisy and he actually.
talks about it for quite a few verses. He gives us three really powerful.
illustrations of how damaging hypocrisy is to our lives as subjects of the.
kingdom. And so we'll be talking about this topic for the next few weeks.
because we're going to go through these these verses. It's a pretty big section. But.
today we're just going to kind of introduce it and scratch the surface..
We're going to look at the first verse of Matthew 6. As usual I have some.
footage for you to look at today. It's hiking footage but I'm going to let you.
know it's not from Cook County. All the other hikes that you've seen in the.
past few weeks have been from Cook County, mostly the forest preserves right.
here around the city of Chicago. And most of them are in southwest Cook County.
because that's close to where I live. But there are places you could get to in 30.
minutes or so from the city. But this week we're going to have something.
different. On the last week of September, Jessamyn and I took the Z's to Great.
Smoky Mountain National Park and we really enjoyed it. We stayed in the North.
Carolina side. It was really quiet there, not many people, easy to social distance.
and it was very peaceful. And we did a lot of hiking with the kids in the park..
So I'm going to share some footage of that with you. But as you see it you'll.
probably see some things you'll say, "Wait a second, I don't think that's anywhere.
around Chicago." It is really beautiful and it was a beautiful time of year to.
be there. And so I just want to encourage you, as I often do, to get outside and.
enjoy God's creation. It's something that's really healthy for us, especially.
during times of uncertainty. And it helps us to connect with God and gives.
us a sense of peace. And this is a great time to do it. Autumn is coming and so.
the trees are changing colors. Everything is really beautiful. So I encourage you.
to do that right here close to home. Find a place with not many people and stay.
safe and wear a mask if you need to. Do whatever you need to do. But get out and.
enjoy God's creation. It's an encouraging and uplifting thing..
Back to Matthew chapter 6. Let's read verse 1 of chapter 6 together. In Matthew.
6 1 Jesus says this, "Beware of practicing your righteousness before.
other people in order to be seen by them. For then you will have no reward from.
your Father who is in heaven." Now as I said, Jesus goes on in this passage to.
give some illustrations of hypocrisy and of what this looks like. But in this.
first verse, Jesus is kind of laying out a general truth about hypocrisy. That we.
should be careful and avoid doing things for people rather than God. Caring about.
what people think of us rather than God. Caring about what the appearance, what.
the image of what we're doing is rather than the reality of our hearts and our.
lives. And that's what Jesus is pointing us to. And I want to call us back real.

$^{41}$quickly as we start to talk about this to the last verse of Matthew chapter 5.
Matthew 5 48. Remember we talked about that verse last week where Jesus says.
you therefore must be perfect as your Heavenly Father is perfect. And we kind.
of scratched the surface of talking about some of our responses to that.
verse. And we spent most of our time last week talking about the right response to.
that verse. The correct response that is to surrender to the fact that we can't.

that's the way that we begin to be who God wants us to be. And we begin to be.
who we want to be. But what I want us to see this week as we start to think about.
what it looks like to avoid hypocrisy in our lives. I want us to see that when we.
are confronted with the fact that we can't live up to God's standard. That we.
are imperfect as humans. That we make mistakes. That we sin. That we fall short..
There are a few different responses we can have. And we mentioned this last week.
but we didn't dig into it as much. And the first response that we could have.
is just kind of a response of rebellion. Basically of saying, "Okay God I don't.

that they fall short. Or maybe they don't even believe that they fall short and.
they say, "You know what I don't think I fall short." But their response is saying,.
"I want to rule my own life. I want to do what I want to do. And I'm not interested.
in listening to God. I'm gonna rebel against whatever God has said in this.

we have probably had at different times in our lives. Where we said, "God I don't.

Another response that we did mention last week is the response of despair..
Just saying, "Well I can't measure up." And really allowing that to call into.
question our self-worth and attacking ourselves and getting to a point of.

and I'm just gonna fall into despair and hopelessness." And obviously that's not.

and to change, to be transformed, to be made into His image. So God doesn't want.

believer. Where we said, "Okay I'm just struggling and I'm not who I want to be..
And I feel hopeless and I want to give up that place of despair." Another.
unhealthy response is this response that Jesus is going to focus on in Matthew.
chapter 6. And that's the response of dishonesty or hypocrisy. And that's when.

$^{81}$we basically say, "You know what? I am going to pretend that I measure up and.
I'm going to tell a lie about the fact that I fall short." And we can tell that.
lie to different people. Sometimes we tell that lie to ourselves and we say,.
"Yeah I don't fall short. I do measure up. I am everything that God wants me to be.
and everything that I want to be." Sometimes we tell that lie to ourselves..
Sometimes we tell it to God. Sometimes we say, "God I don't need you in my life.
because I'm good enough on my own." But sometimes we tell it to other people and.
we try to put forward this image that we are something that we're not. We try to.
put forward this perception, this illusion that we are keeping God's law.
and we're living right and we're doing all the right things in life even when.
that's not the reality of our heart. And that's a pretty good working definition.
of what hypocrisy is. Hypocrisy is when we are pretending, when we are acting,.
when we are giving off an image or creating some illusion that we are.
something that we're not. And when we're pretending to be something we're not..
When we're pretending to be someone that we're not. That's when we fall into.
hypocrisy. And we know that hypocrisy is so hurtful, it's so damaging. And.
hypocrisy in relationship to our faith and our following of Jesus is probably.
some of the most damaging of all because it causes people to just discard God's.
truth. And people look at someone's life who's hypocritical and they say, "Well you.
know there's some things there, I've heard some truth about Jesus that.
maybe I might be interested in but then I see hypocrisy in someone's life and it.
just turns me away. I just want to discard, even the good things, I.
don't want to listen to them anymore because of hypocrisy." And so we know it.
can be really unhealthy and we've probably all been hurt by it in our.
lives. We've probably been hurt by someone who held us to some standard.
or told us that we were supposed to be a certain way but then they didn't live.
that out themselves. And their words and their actions didn't agree and that.
hypocrisy, that dissonance bothered us and hurt us and made us upset. We've.
probably all experienced that. And the reality is all of us as humans are.
hypocrites. We've all acted out hypocrisy. All of us have. It's something that's.
easy for me to talk about because I'm an expert in it. We all are experts in.
hypocrisy. We're all really good at pretending to be something we're not..
We're all really good at trying to make other people think that we are someone.
that we are not in our heart and on the inside. It's something that all of us do..
And last week we talked about the one right response to Matthew 5:48 and that.
is that response to surrender. We really covered that last week so I'm not going.
to get into it again but I just want to draw one thing as we move on this week.
and that is the fact that surrendering to God and allowing Jesus to live.
through us is really a journey and not a destination and that's so important for.
us to understand. And it's important that we understand that in order to avoid.

$^{121}$hypocrisy in our life because sometimes as followers of Jesus, as Christians, as.
subjects of the kingdom, we can think that surrender is a destination. That we.
get there once and once we've arrived that we're there for the rest of our.
life. That we get there and we say, "God, I'm gonna surrender. I'm gonna give it all.

happens when we have some type of experience in church where God really.
moves on our heart and we say, "Okay God, I'm gonna surrender everything to you.".
And those are beautiful moments and yes when that surrender happens it's real.
and it's complete but we still have this natural part of us, what the.
scripture calls the old man or the flesh, this part of us that's still.
really selfish and really sinful and that part of us fights against the.
spiritual part of us. The New Testament talks about this and that part of us.
wants to grab control back that we surrender to God. And so we don't just.
surrender once. It's not something that we get to that point and we surrender.
and then we never have to surrender again. No, we have to surrender and we.
have to surrender over and over again. It's a journey. It's a constant.
journey of surrender. We have to daily surrender to God's control and moment by.
moment when that part of us rises up and says, "No, I want to be selfish and I want.
to focus on me and I want to do what's right for me instead of trying to obey.
God." We have to surrender again and again and again throughout life. And that.
process, that journey in church, a lot of times people call it sanctification. It's.
just a big church word that means that we're becoming more like Christ..
And as we continue to surrender, that's what happens. As we surrender more and.
more of our life and we surrender in those areas that we struggle in again.
and again, we begin to become more like Christ. We begin to be more of who God.
wants us to be and more of who we want to be. And our behavior changes, our.
attitudes change, the way we treat other people changes. Those things happen, but.
it's a process. It's not just a destination. And so if you find yourself.

of surrender whereby we continue to walk in those things. We continue to repent of.
our sin. We continue to give control to Jesus and we continue to release control.
from our own hands. We continue to try to abide in Him like we talked about last.
week in John 15. It's a journey. It's a process. And that's important for us to.
know because sometimes in the church we say, "Well, I surrendered. I think I'm done..
I've got it all figured out." And we start to walk in our own strength again. And.
once we do that, we start to fall into hypocrisy. We start to become someone who.
is acting like we're something that we're not. So today as we kind of.

$^{161}$introduce and think about hypocrisy, I want us to think about a few kind of big.
ideas about hypocrisy and maybe they'll help us to be aware of it in our.
life and to avoid it. And the first thing I want us to think about is why we're.

it. And I think the biggest reason that we're tempted towards hypocrisy, if we're.
honest with ourselves, is pride. We don't want to believe that we fall short of.
God's standard. We don't want to believe that we're something less than who we.
want to be. We don't want to believe that we're something less than perfect. And we.
