So as you do that, in street parking in Chicago, you pay attention to the signs, right? 那你在我們家街趴的時候,我們肯定要看路牌嘛..
So I was on the street in Hyde Park, and one side, they have this orange paper sign, you know, tied on the trees, right? 那我在樹上看到橘色的一個紙牌..
And then on this side, it says no parking on Monday. 那我在樹上看到橘色的一個牌子,掛在那裡..
They are doing street cleaning. 要一邊寫著禮拜一不準停車..
And then on the other side, you know, they also hang some signs, right? And there is no parking, the sign says no parking on Tuesday. 嗯,他們要洗街..
And that day was Monday. 那天是禮拜一..
And then I thought, very simple, okay, I find an empty spot, and that day was Monday, yes. 然後我就想,非常簡單,我找到一個空的地方,那天是星期一..
I find a parking space on one side of the street, so I park on the Tuesday side, and I'm safe. 我找到一條街道上的停車位,所以我停在週一那邊,我安全了..
So I parked the car and I left, and I came back a few hours later. 那我先講很簡單嘛,今天是禮拜一,那我應該趴在禮拜二那邊..
我終於千辛萬苦找到個位子在禮拜二那邊,應該沒有問題..
So I parked the car and I left, and I came back a few hours later, and there was an orange citation, one orange envelope on the windshield. 那幾個小時以後呢,我發現一個橘色的信封在我的車窗上面..
And then what happened was that when I was looking for a parking space, and I checked the signs, and I got confused. 那結果是我自己看多了兩邊的路牌以後,我自己覺得路牌..
So it was Monday, I should park on the which side? 禮拜一的話,我應該趴在哪一邊?.
Not parking on Tuesday side, right? 應該是趴在禮拜二不準趴車那邊..
That's what I thought I did. 那應該是這樣子想的,對吧?.
But I was wrong, I did not pay attention that I was actually parking on the no parking on Monday side. 但是我趴在了錯誤的那一邊,我趴在了禮拜一不準趴車那邊..
So I got that orange envelope, and my first reaction was that this is so unfair. 我一拿到橘色的信封,我就覺得這太不公平了..
And then you feel like the law is out to get me, you know? 這個法律是要用來整我的嗎?.
Have you ever got something like that before? 你有沒有這樣的感覺?.
Anyone? 任何人?.
拿到了一個信封以後,太不公平了..
The city of Chicago is evil. 芝加哥政府太糟糕了..
Or maybe I was confused, you know? 也許是我自己迷糊了..
But that's our modern conception or modern feeling about law. 這是我們大多數人對法律的感覺..

$^{41}$Now when we go to the Old Testament, we see commandments and rules, we sometimes read them the same way. 當我們看到舊約的時候,我們看到這樣的一些律法,我們是有相似的感覺..
So you feel like that, right? You open the Bible, you look at the laws, and there are some details, a lot of commandments, ten commandments, and you feel like God is, you know, like a traffic police, you know, okay? 這樣的感覺,對吧?你打開了詩書,看了法律,看了一些細節,有很多的命令,十個命令..
You feel like God is, you know, like a traffic police, you know, okay? 這樣的感覺,對吧?你感覺像是一名交通警察,你知道嗎?.
Always out to get you, you know? 總是要用法律來整你,你知道嗎?.
And then you feel like that, right? 當我們翻開舊約的時候,有些感覺,有些時候會想,神是不是就像那個交通督導員,.
就是要抓我們的錯誤,你們就被罰款了. And then you feel like that, right? 當我們翻開舊約的時候,有些感覺,有些時候會想,神是不是就像那個交通督導員,就是要抓我們的錯誤,你們就被罰款了..
But I want to suggest to you, maybe we have misread the sign. 但我想在這裡要大家想一想,是不是我們一直看錯了路牌呢?.
So I want to show you from the Bible, from the Old Testament itself, the law was never designed to catch us, but it's to show us a better way to live. 所以我想在這裡要大家想一想,是不是我們一直看錯了路牌呢?.
這也想告訴你的是,律法從來不需要抓我們的把柄,而是要指引我們的道路..
See, from this PowerPoint slide, you can see the common misreading or misunderstanding is that the Old Testament, you know, is full of law, rules and judgment. 從這個 PowerPoint 圖上可以看到,律法從來不需要抓我們的把柄,而是要指引我們的道路..
那我們常見有幾個誤解,就像我們 PowerPoint 下面所講的,就是舊約常常讓人覺得是關於律法,規條和審判的..
And then we flip to the pages on the New Testament, and we feel like, oh, it's all about grace and all about freedom and love. 然後我們翻到新約的頁面,我們覺得,哦,這全都是關於恩典,愛和自由..
But, you know, this is a misreading of the whole Bible. 但是,你們知道,這是整個讀書的錯誤..
這絕對是一種誤解..
So, I want to begin with the first point is that the first thing you need to understand about law is that it is of grace. 那,律法其實是關於恩典的律法..
Now, the truth is that, you know, the law was never the opposite of grace, the law was actually grace. 律法從來不是恩典的對立面,律法本身就是恩典..
Now, as some of you know, I'm leaving tonight, I'm flying to Turkey, and I'm leading a group to Turkey in the next two weeks. 現在,有些網友知道,我今天晚上會帶領一個團隊前往土耳其..
Now, you probably have some, you know, a concept that when I mention Turkey, what kind of Bible stories you can think of? 那可能如果你熟悉聖經的話,將我講到土耳其,大家會想到聖經的哪一個部分?.
Probably all in the New Testament, right? Paul's missionary journeys, and the seven churches of the book of Revelation. 可能都是關於新約的保羅的宣教旅程,啟示錄的七個教會等等..
But, you know, Turkey was actually the heartland of the Old Testament. 但是,土耳其也是舊約的核心地帶..
Because in the Old Testament time, the same place, Turkey was the homeland for ancient superpower called Hittite Kingdom. 因為在舊約時期,土耳其是古代世界最強大的帝國之一的故鄉,赫人帝國..
So, what the people have found in the capital of the ancient Hittite Kingdom was what we call a suzerain treaty. 當科普學家挖掘到這個帝國的遺址的時候,發現很多的泥板,其中的一個我們叫做宗教條約..
And then, these kind of treaties are actually treaty between a great nation or great king like Hittite King, the great king, between the great king and the small kingdom. 然後,這種條約是大國與附屬小國之間所立的條約..
And what is interesting is, every single this kind of document, it follows the same format. 每一種宗主的條約其實都用同樣的格式..
So, as you can see here, number one, the treaty begins with the introduction of the great king. 第一個部分,基本上是一個大王來用很長的篇幅來介紹自己有多偉大有多偉大..
So, after the preamble is the second part, which is what we call the historical introduction or prologue. 第二個部分我們叫做是歷史的序言..
And the great king will say something to the small kingdom and say, this is what I have done for you guys before. 那這個很大的偉大的國王就會說,這是我已經為你做的事情..
Perhaps some years before the treaty, the great king has saved this small nation from military attack. 可能很久很久之前你們被人攻打的時候,我來拯救了你們..
So, the historical prologue is to remind the small kingdom that I have been good to you. 那這個部分基本上是用來提醒他們我曾經對你們做過恩典的事情..
And then the number three part, part three is the stipulations or the laws. 第三個部分就是關於律法條款..
So, the stipulations or the laws are saying because I have been gracious to you, and that's why you have to live this way in response. 那這個部分基本上是說因為我如此的恩典的待遇,你應該如何的去回應我如何去生活..
And then number four is the blessing and the curses. 第四個部分關於祝福與詛咒..
So, the treaty says if you obey me, if you are faithful to me, then I will bless you, I will be good to you. 那它說忠誠,我就會給你祝福..
But if you are rebellious, then there will be consequences. 那如果你叛逆我的話,也會帶來後果的..
Now, you look at this format of the Suzerain Treaty, you find it very interesting because it's very similar to the Old Testament law. 那如果你看這個宗主條約的話,你會發現跟我們舊約非常相像..
So, when we go to the Ten Commandments, for example, Exodus 20, 如果你看到埃及紀第20章,我們的十件,.
and before any single so-called commandment begins, it gives you these verses. 那首先在什麼其他東西都不用講的同時,它首先跟你講這句話..
So, let me read this. I am the Lord your God, 我是耶和華你的神, who brought you out of Egypt, out of the land of slavery. 曾將你從埃及帝為奴之家領出來..
Now, only then, after this, do we find the commandments or Ten Commandments. 那這個之後,我們纔會發現十約..
And then the Ten Commandments do not begin with obey me, so I will love you. 十約並不是開始的時候怎麼說,你順從我,然後我再愛你,不是這樣開始的..

$^{81}$It's the other way around. It begins with I have already loved you, I have already rescued you, and here is how you live as my people now. 而是我已經拯救了你,現在這是你做我子民的生活方式..
So, grace comes first, the rescue came first, and then the law came second. The law is flowing out of grace. 拯救在前,律法在後,律法是從恩典流出的..
So, you have to understand, you have to erase the wrong impression. Law is given to you, is to trick you, is to punish you. 你要把這個否定的那個想法,關於律法的想法給去掉..
So, grace first, and then the law is to teach you and guide you how you live. 恩典是先在律法之前出現,然後律法來指導你如何生活..
And then the second aspect of the law in the Old Testament especially is actually wisdom. 第二個方面是關於智慧的..
So, the law reveals the heart of God, the wisdom of God. 律法揭示了神的心腸..
Now, what do the specific laws actually look like? 那些具體的律法究竟是怎麼樣的呢?.
Now, you may have some impression, but I want to show you two examples. 我想給你兩個例子..
So, besides the Ten Commandments, the popular, you know, everybody knows, but I want to give you two samples from some of the laws in the Old Testament. 除了十節以外,我想給你兩個例子..
So, let's take a look at this one, from Deuteronomy 22. 申命記二十二章第八節..
So, pay attention as I read it. So, pay attention as I read it. 小姐,請你們注意..
So, Moses is trying, is to giving the law to the people of God, to Israel, he says, when you build a new house, make a parapet around your roof, so that you may not bring guilt of bloodshed on your house if someone falls from the roof. 你建造新房子,要在房頂上安欄杆,.
免得有人從房上掉下來,流血的罪就歸你家了. So, that's interesting, this law is actually building code. 這很奇怪,這是關於如何建造房子的..
It tells you how to build a house. 你怎麼樣建造一個房子..
Now, in ancient Israel, the house had flat roof. 在古代的以色列,屋頂是平坦的..
So, people can go up to the roof and do something to work there. So, God is saying, you know, when you build a house, you have to build railing, you know, some sort of barrier, so that, you know, perhaps, you know, a child goes up there, and he will fall from the roof. 因為屋頂是平坦的話,人們就可以爬上去做各樣的事情..
那神說要安欄杆,可能就讓孩子不會墜落..
Yeah, anyone has done renovation in your house lately? 有沒有人裝修的,在家裡?.
Okay, a lot, right? And you have to watch out for safety, right? 你們要注意安全,對?.
So, this law is actually a safety law. 那這個關於安全的律法..
But the law, behind the law, reveals the wisdom or the heart of God. 但是律法告訴了我們..
So, it's like the heavenly Father saying, you know, life is sacred, life is so special, and God wants to protect life, and so no one, even when no one is watching. 這是一位父親講的話,生命是神聖的,要保護它,即便沒有人在看..
So, you see that the law is trying to reveal to you the heart of God, the wisdom of God. 這關於神的智慧以及神的心腸..
Now, the second example I want to show you is from Leviticus, chapter 19. 這是下一個是關於歷位紀十九章第十九節..
Do not reap the very edges of your field, or gather the gleanings of your harvest, leave them for the poor and for the foreigner. 你們收割莊稼不可割盡田角,也不可拾取所遺落的,要留給窮人和寄居的外人..
So, you may say this is a harvest law, a harvest code. 可能關於是如何收割的一個規定..
So, your harvest is your entire livelihood, right? 你的收成是你全年的生計..
Whether you have wheat or barley or whatever, God is trying to say to you in this law is saying, when you harvest your wheat and barley, your produce, you have to leave the edges out. 神說你收割莊稼的時候,你必須要留下田角..
So, there are some, you know, some of your production, your food items, you have to leave behind for the widows, for the foreigners. 你要為寡婦,孤兒,陌生人留下可以喫的..
So, you see, this law is kind of a very tiny thing, you know, a very tiny thing about, you know, how you live. 這些都是關於生活的很小的一些關鍵..
But as you can see, you know, when you harvest, you don't harvest every single thing. 但是你收成不是收聖所有的東西..
So, you leave it to the weak people or the poor in the society, so they come after you, they can pick up those food. 你還要去照顧社會上面的底層的人民..
And this is the heart of God, this is justice, it's building kind of building a society, economic system, so that, you know, when you look at this law, it's actually the value from God, behind every value is that, you know, God is trying to protect the weak. 這是建立經濟制度本身之中的公益,每一條律法背後都有一個價值觀,而每一個價值觀背後都有一個神要保護的人..
And this is exactly what I'm saying, you know, the wisdom of God, the heart of God is written in everyday life of the people of God. 這就是神的智慧寫進了日常生活之中..
So, the law is actually grace, and the law is actually revealing the heart of God, the wisdom of God, and number three, the law were meant to be missional, to have the world to see how you live. 律法也是關於使命的..
So, we have to ask the question, why the law was given to Israel, to the people of God, what was the ultimate point? 那麼為什麼要把這些律法賜給以色列呢?它最終的目的是什麼呢?.
Deuteronomy 4 says, again Moses is talking to the people of God before they enter the land of Canaan, and he says, observe them, observe those laws that I have preached to you, I have told you, observe them carefully, this will show your wisdom to the nations, to the pagan nations, and they will say, surely, this is how they live, this great nation is a wise and understanding people..
So, the laws in the Old Testament are actually public display of your life, you know, kind of a new way of life, a new way of life that is marked by justice, by the law. 摩西在以進入以色列,進入應許之地之前說,你們要謹守遵行,這就是你們在萬民眼前的智慧,聰明,他們聽見這一切的律例必說,這大國的人真是有智慧,有聰明..
So, the laws in the Old Testament are actually public display of your life, you know, kind of a new way of life, a new way of life that is marked by justice, by generosity, by grace to the surrounding nations, and the surrounding nations will get curious about, hey, this is how you live, you live different than us, and who is your God, and we want to know Him as well. 摩西在以進入以色列,進入應許之地之前說,你們要謹守遵行,這就是你們在萬民眼前的智慧,聰明,他們聽見這一切的律例必說,這大國的人真是有智慧,有聰明..
所以,律法是公開的見證,一種公義恩慈的生活方式,使周圍的國家都會問,他們的神是誰呢,我想認識他..

$^{121}$今天是我們的,這是我們的護照,我們透過日常的生活的智力,見證神的美善,誠實,慷慨,以及我們對待那些無法回報我們的人的一些方式..
這不是一個新的策略,如果我們在古代發現,這不是一個新的策略,而是聖經裡面最古老的一個生活方式..
實踐是神親自用手指把它刻在石頭上的..
《出埃及記》31章,它說,他將兩塊法板交給摩西,是神用指頭寫的石板..
這不是一份可以隨便修改的備忘錄,而是刻在石頭上的盟約,永遠的長存..
那我們就是為什麼我要你帶一個這樣的小瓶子回家呢?.
我們這個小瓶子裡面裝著沙子..
在第一個部分,這個講到第二部分,我們講到了神對亞伯拉罕的應許,神用亞伯拉罕去祝福萬國的人..
第二個部分,我給你們什麼了呢?是一塊拼圖..
上一次我們跟你說,亞伯拉罕這一堆人全部都是破碎的人..
但是上帝選擇用他們去祝福萬國..
他們的神是我們一樣的神..
今天我要請你們把一些石頭帶回家..
希望你們今天結束的時候,拿一些石頭可以放在你的袋子裡面,帶回家..
當你握住這些石頭的時候,請記住,神把律法刻在石頭上,因為祂的信息是永恆的..
這石頭提醒我們,神說我已經拯救了你,我如此的愛你,這是你應當如何生活的方式..
把它放在家裡某個你可以看到的地方,讓它每天問你一個問題..
我的生活方式有沒有讓人對我的神感到好奇呢?.
神不是要我們完美地活著,但是神要求我們忠實地活著..
這是一個邀請,活得如此的有智慧,如此的慷慨,讓一個旁觀者的世界渴望認識這一切背後的善意..
要知道,實踐是從拯救開始的,一直是如此,我們的福音也是如此..
請幫助我們接受禰的律法,不是覺得它是一種威脅,而是一種禮物..
願我們的生活方式使人渴望認識禰..
奉耶穌的名求,給你們..
我今晚要飛,請祈禱我和我的團隊,我們有17個人要去土耳其..
我會盡力更新您的信息,這取決於互聯網,我會在土耳其錄製一些視頻..
下個禮拜見!.

[NON-ENGLISH SPEECH].

and they follow me..

$^{1}$[NON-ENGLISH SPEECH].
Good morning, brothers and sisters..
[NON-ENGLISH SPEECH].

[NON-ENGLISH SPEECH].
It's about not just a name, but life..
[NON-ENGLISH SPEECH].
Therefore, a prisoner for the Lord.
urge you to walk in a manner worthy of the calling.
to which you have been called..

with patience, bearing with one another in love,.

in the bond of peace..

Before we begin, let me ask you to imagine a scene..
Suppose you walk into the Michelin three-star restaurant..
At the entrance, you see the prestigious Michelin.
certification displayed proudly..
The interior is elegant and luxurious..
Every waiter is dressed sharply in suit,.
and everything just feels professional..
[NON-ENGLISH SPEECH].

Instant noodle soup in plain hot water.

So you freeze..

$^{41}$[NON-ENGLISH SPEECH].
You call the manager and ask, wait a minute..

We carry the identity of citizen of heaven..
We carry the label Christian..

Today, we will look at this passage in three parts..
First, those who are called must remember their identity..
Second, those who are called must live out.
the character of Christ..
And third, those who are called must diligently preserve unity..
[NON-ENGLISH SPEECH].
Paul says in verse 1, "I, therefore,.
a prisoner for the Lord, urge you.
to walk in a manner worthy of this calling to which you.
have been called.".
This is a major turning point in the whole book of Ephesians..
What did Paul spend the first three chapters talking about?.
He talked about how Father chose us, how Christ redeemed us,.
how did the Holy Spirit seal us, and once we were dead in sin..

$^{81}$Well, now we have life..

to talk about how should we live..

This is the logic of our gospel..
Grace comes first..
Response comes second..
Identity comes first..
Lifestyle comes second..
God always acts first..
And then we respond..
God moves first, and then we follow..
This is the gospel..
[NON-ENGLISH SPEECH].
Now compare what other religions in the world says..
What do they say?.
They will say, fix yourself first..
You have to do your part better first..

The gospel says, God loves you when you are still unworthy..

[NON-ENGLISH SPEECH].
There is another reason Paul waits until chapter 4.
to talk about Christian living..
Paul knows this..
It's so true that if you don't know who you are,.

Without gospel and doctrine, what's.
left here or in Christianity?.
When you are told to try hard and better.
and become a better person, that is not gospel..
That is moral advice..
[NON-ENGLISH SPEECH].
And this world always has plenty of moral advice..
When we are in trouble, we always.
focus solely on changing the outside circumstances.

$^{121}$or our behavior, and we miss the root issue--.
understanding the gospel..
Why do we become jealous?.
Why do we fight?.
Why do we hurt each other?.
Because we forgot who we are..
We forgot that we are the people of grace..
[NON-ENGLISH SPEECH].
That's why Paul waits until chapter 4.
to start talking about how we should live..
[NON-ENGLISH SPEECH].

What does that actually mean?.
It means we did not find God first by ourselves..
God calls us first, just like Lazarus..

[NON-ENGLISH SPEECH].
So what he actually means here--.

$^{161}$Imagine Pastor Mark got drunk every day,.

Next, let's look at the second point..

we have received..
